citation.authors: Cormier JN, Xing Y, Ding M, Lee JE et al

cited_by.title: Skin cancer and moles on dark skin

record.population: 251 African Americans and 48,143 White patients with melanoma, SEER registry, 1992-2002
record.finding: Melanoma incidence was 0.8 per 100,000 in African Americans against 18.4 in White people. African Americans were 4.2 times as likely to present at stage IV. Overall 5-year survival was 72.2% to 81.1% for minorities against 89.6% for White patients.

record.population: 251 African Americans and 48,143 White patients with melanoma in the US cancer registry (SEER), 1992-2002
record.finding: Melanoma incidence was 0.8 per 100,000 in African Americans against 18.4 in White people. African Americans were 4.2 times as likely to present at stage IV, and had a 1.48-fold higher risk-adjusted, stage-specific mortality. Overall 5-year survival was 72.2% to 81.1% for minorities against 89.6% for White patients.
record.note: Registry data; melanoma is rare in Black people, but is found later. This study does not say sunscreen prevents melanoma in Black people, and it does not test sun exposure as a cause.
